note: Realistic filled-in states in the scoring engine's shape. `expected` is computed by `bin/test-personas --update` and verified by `bin/test-personas`. This engine's suitability axis has three bands (ok/caution/limited); both caution and limited raise the same F-PREP-NOT-MET-001 flag (with different wording), but only 'limited' (unflagged prep alone stays 'caution') forces the distinctive `redirect` recommendation.

personas.name: emergency-suspected-aaa-abdomen-fasting-not-flagged-caution
personas.description: Sudden severe back and abdominal pain with a pulsatile abdominal mass: an abdominal ultrasound is the recommended (ideal) examination for the suspected-aaa indication, and the red flag itself auto-escalates triage to emergency regardless of the routine urgency requested; there was no time to fast the patient, so the request does not flag fasting required even though an abdominal scan usually needs it — this forces a suitability caution (not the more severe 'limited' band), which is non-blocking — expect usually-appropriate + caution suitability + emergency + accept.

personas.name: redirect-abdominal-pain-abdomen-high-bmi-limited-incomplete
personas.description: Vague generalised abdominal discomfort in a patient with a raised BMI: an abdominal ultrasound is itself the recommended (ideal) examination for the abdominal-pain indication — there is no appropriateness mismatch, and fasting is correctly flagged — but a BMI of 38 (>= the 35 body-habitus threshold) on this deep region independently forces the suitability band to 'limited', which is this engine's distinctive trigger for the `redirect` recommendation ('Redirect / amend preparation'), overriding the 'ok' fasting outcome directly rather than just adding a caution; several administrative fields are not yet captured — expect usually-appropriate + limited suitability + routine + redirect, completeness below 100.
